case.question: Any netball venues in Reservoir 3073 with accessible parking within 250 m?
case.note: 250 m is the facility band, not a venue radius; the answer must not say no venue lies within 250 m.

result.answer:
Yes — 8 netball venues in the Reservoir 3073 area match accessible parking at the venue, per the Sport and Recreational Facilities List (last updated 2024-12-17). The three closest:

- Darebin Community Sports Stadium, Reservoir — parking "At the venue, per Sport and Recreational Facilities List." (2667 m)
- H P Zwar Reserve, Preston — same wording (3276 m)
- Martin Reserve, Hadfield — same wording (4393 m)

Distances are straight-line metres from the centre of Reservoir.

Four more venues have no published information on parking, check with the venue; two say it is not available. Full list: /venues/DAREBI11808

case.question: Is there a tennis program for people who are blind or have low vision?

result.answer:
Yes. The publisher AAA Play writes that the Blind Tennis Program uses "various types of balls, including audible tennis balls and different sized and coloured balls", and that "people of all ages and backgrounds can join". The adult program runs as a six-week program on Friday nights during school terms; there is also a junior program for ages 5 to 15.

It's listed at Melbourne Sports & Aquatic Centre, Albert Park. Published access there: accessible toilet 73 m away and accessible change facility 73 m away (straight line, National Public Toilet Map, updated 2022-01-12); nearest recorded accessible parking 1381 m, beyond the 500 m limit (City of Melbourne); no published information on an accessible transport stop, check with the venue.

Separately, Doncaster Tennis Club says its coaches run programs for blind or low vision players. Details: /events/DS-09:activity:20905

case.question: Which programs mention audible tennis balls?

result.answer:
One program mentions them: the Blind Tennis Program. The publisher writes that they "use various types of balls, including audible tennis balls and different sized and coloured balls."

The same publisher describes an adult six-week program during school terms on Friday nights at the National Tennis Centre on indoor courts, run by Blind Sports & Recreation Victoria, Tennis Victoria and Tennis Seniors Victoria, and a Junior Blind Tennis program for kids aged 5 to 15 who are blind or have vision problems.

case.question: Is there a unified football program for young people with disability run with Melbourne Victory?

result.answer:
Yes. The publisher, AAA Play, writes that the "Melbourne Victory All Abilities Unified Football Program" is "for young people with disability or additional support needs", offering "a fun, safe, and welcoming place to play football, learn new skills, make friends, and have fun."

They list four sessions:
- Ages 6–16 and 12–18: 17 October – 5 December, 10:30am–11:20am (/events/DS-09:activity:25162)
- Ages 16+: 14 October – 16 December, bi-weekly, 11:00am–12:00pm (/events/DS-09:activity:25160)
- Ages 6–16 and 16+: 16 October – 4 December, 5:00pm–5:50pm (/events/DS-09:activity:25161)
- The Melbourne Victory All Abilities Football Centre in Fawkner (/events/DS-09:activity:25033)

These are the publisher's own words; check their page to join.
